claims.text: At stage-3 DonHang.App's lib/ is split by kind: screens/, widgets/, offline/, auth/, plus models.dart, providers.dart, api_client.dart. Ordering code (order screens, order shapes, orderProvider, order API calls, the queue) sits in five of these, each also holding code that products or sign-in use.
claims.source_hint: docs/design/app-structure.md @ stage-4 lines 7-10; git ls-tree stage-3 DonHang.App/lib; lib/providers.dart, models.dart, api_client.dart @ stage-3

claims.text: From stage-4 lib/ is split by feature: each folder under lib/features/ (auth/, catalog/, ordering/) is one job the app does for the customer, with that job's screens, providers, models and API calls.
claims.source_hint: docs/design/app-structure.md @ stage-4 lines 11-20; STAGE.md @ stage-4 lines 30-31

claims.text: features/ordering/ at stage-4 holds eight files: create_order_screen, order (OrderItemRequest, OrderResult, totalVnd), order_detail_screen, order_queue, ordering (public file), orders_api (ordersApiProvider, orderProvider, fetchOrder, createOrder), queue_sync, queued_orders_screen.

claims.text: Stage-3 origins: the three order screens were in screens/, order shapes in models.dart, fetchOrder/createOrder in api_client.dart, orderProvider in providers.dart, order_queue/queue_sync in offline/; local_store.dart and browser*.dart moved from offline/ to shared/.
claims.source_hint: git ls-tree stage-3 vs stage-4 DonHang.App/lib; STAGE.md @ stage-4 lines 258-261

claims.text: shared/ holds the HTTP transport that catalog and ordering use (api_client.dart: API address, token header sent by ordering's calls) and on-device storage (local_store.dart) with its browser wrapper; auth imports none of it; design/ holds the design system and all three features import it.
claims.source_hint: app-structure.md @ stage-4 lines 21-22; imports of ../../shared/ and ../../design/ under lib/features @ stage-4

claims.text: main.dart and router.dart belong to no feature and assemble the features, the job a composition root does for DonHang.Api; main.dart imports design/brand.dart, design/theme.dart, features/ordering/ordering.dart, l10n/app_localizations.dart, router.dart and starts the queue sync.

router.dart imports features/auth/auth.dart, features/catalog/catalog.dart and features/ordering/ordering.dart and gives each screen a path; no file under lib/features imports main.dart or router.dart.
claims.source_hint: DonHang.App/lib/router.dart @ stage-4 lines 5-11, 43-69; grep imports under lib/features @ stage-4

claims.text: Two app features carry DonHang.Api module names: Catalog (DonHang.Catalog) and Ordering (DonHang.Domain, DonHang.Infrastructure); the team's word leads to code on both sides. Auth has no backend module: sign-in is Keycloak's job, the app only keeps the token.

A single screen that serves an existing feature goes into that feature; a new feature is added for a new job for the customer that changes for its own reasons, and needs a row in the doc's dependency table.

Feature folders pay off when several features change for different reasons; an app with one or two screens gains little and can be grouped by kind; copying HTTP/design code into each feature makes copies drift and is rarely worth it.
Layout decides how many places a change touches; a screen changes with its provider, model and API call, so grouping all screens together makes the rest harder to find as the app grows.
